# Recorded output of real ZFS tools

Every file here is the verbatim stdout+stderr of one real command, run against a real ZFS pool on
OpenZFS 2.4.1 (`zfs-2.4.1-1ubuntu5.1`, `zfs-kmod-2.4.1-1ubuntu5`) on Linux 7.0. The first line of
each file is the command; the last is `[exit <status>]`.

They exist because spec v0.6 §54.4 asks for real ZFS where the environment permits, and because a
provider whose parser has only ever seen output somebody wrote by hand has not been tested. The
deterministic suite replays these bytes through `ono_change_core::ScriptedRunner`; the gated
real-filesystem suite runs the same code against a live pool.

Regenerated by `scripts/fs-fixtures.sh`, which builds the pool from nothing in a disposable
container. Do not hand-edit a file here: an edit is a claim about what ZFS prints, and the whole
point is that nobody is making claims.

The layout the fixtures were taken against:

```text
rpool                       /rpool
rpool/ROOT                  /altroot
rpool/ROOT/debian           /altroot/debian
tank                        /tank
tank/data                   /tank/data
tank/data/customer          /tank/data/customer      8 MiB of data
tank/home                   /tank/home
tank/cloned                 /tank/cloned             clone of tank/data@ono-b91c-...
```

with snapshots `rpool/ROOT/debian@ono-a82f-20260909T194500Z`, `rpool/ROOT/debian@later-1`,
a recursive `tank/data@ono-b91c-20260909T194501Z`, and a bookmark `rpool/ROOT/debian#book-1`.

`rollback-refused.txt` is the one to read first. It is what ZFS actually says when a rollback would
have to destroy newer history, and §13.6 forbids Ono adding the flag that makes it stop saying it.
